author: Reuters
title: Australian, NZ shares in the red as growth fears rattle global markets By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. Australian, NZ shares in the red as growth fears rattle global markets * Wall Street slides on Apple's revenue forecast cut
* Aussie insurers lead losses among financials
* Gold prices gain as uncertainty sparks safety bets
By Nikhil Nainan
Jan 4 (Reuters) - Australian shares slid on Friday, tracking moves on Wall Street, which fell sharply after weak U.S. data and Apple's revenue warning stoked fears about the outlook for the global economy.
The S&P/ASX 200 index .AXJO fell 1.1 percent, or 61.2 points, to 5,572.2 by 0023 GMT, and is set to end a holiday-shortened week 1.1 percent lower.
Apple AAPL.O blamed its lowered revenue forecast for the holiday quarter on sales in China, ratcheting fears that Australia's largest trading partner is being dragged under by the uncertainty of the Sino-U.S. trade battle. surprise cut comes at a time of increasing concern that growth in China is slowing at a sharper pace than many expected.
Financial stocks .AXFJ fell 1.2 percent, with insurers leading the losses. Suncorp Group SUN.AX fell as much as 2.5 percent to its biggest intraday percentage drop in two weeks.
On Thursday, Suncorp said it expects the total natural hazard costs across Australia and New Zealand to well exceed the amount it made allowances for in the half-year ended Dec. 31.
Mathan Somasundaram, a Blue Ocean Equities market portfolio strategist, said the Australian summer has so far been bad for insurers with claims from natural hazards and other events likely.
Suncorp's peers, Insurance Australia Group IAG.AX and QBE Insurance Group QBE.AX fell 2.1 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
Mirroring broad-based losses on the benchmark, resource stocks .AXMM dropped 1.4 percent with global miners BHP BHP.AX and Rio Tinto (LON: RIO ) RIO.AX both down around 2 percent.
In the other direction, global growth worries fuelled safe-haven bets in the form of gold stocks. Australian gold miners reaped the benefits, with the sub-index .AXGD up 1.5 percent. GOL/
Newcrest Mining NCM.AX and St Barbara SBM.AX gained 2.5 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
In the healthcare space, Healius Ltd HLS.AX was 2.7 percent higher after it received a A$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion) offer on Thursday from Chinese construction company and top shareholder Jangho Group Co Ltd 601886.SS . at A$2.705 per share at 0023 GMT, the stock was still below Jangho's indicative offer price of A$3.25.
Blue Ocean Equities' Somasundaram said investors are not optimistic that the deal will go through, despite the gains. He added that an offer closer to A$4 would be more compelling for investors.
In its second session of 2019, New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index .NZ50 lost 0.5 percent to 8,693.34.
Index heavyweight a2 Milk Company ATM.NZ weighed on the benchmark, falling 4.1 percent to a near two week low.
